{"type":"text","timestamp":1794628684945,"sessionID":"ses_e27ce130cffevKOw46UlfTQT1S","part":{"id":"prt_1d8348c87001xjiyPW61jle7bF","messageID":"msg_1d8346a0a001UNKwo75hNTMKQd","sessionID":"ses_e27ce130cffevKOw46UlfTQT1S","type":"text","text":"The episode has ended. The rover finished at base with about 9.5 battery left, so the base multiplier is 1.0.\n\n**Expected score: about 6 / 13 ≈ 0.46.** It collected 6 points of the 13 available across all targets, including the two discovered during the mission.\n\n| Target | Value | Result |\n|---|---|---|\n| t1 | 2 | Sampled at tick 5, on time |\n| t5 | 2 | Sampled at tick 7, on time (deadline 13) |\n| t2 | 2 | Sampled at tick 26, on time (deadline 30) |\n| t4 | 1 | Missed: both sample attempts failed |\n| t3 | 1 | Skipped, not enough energy |\n| d2 (discovered) | 3 | Skipped: it fit the time but would have left about 1 unit of battery spare |\n| d1 (discovered) | 2 | Skipped: impossible before its deadline at tick 28, and too costly late |\n\n**What went wrong:**\n- **I planned the t4 drives too early.** I queued all the sand driving toward t4 before I had measured how much the wheels slip on sand. I assumed about 0.33; it was actually about 0.2. The rover went about 1.4 m past t4 and the sample at tick 12 failed. The correction then landed about 0.85 m short, outside the 0.75 m sampling radius, so the second sample failed too.\n- **Sand drained the battery.** About 15 wheel-metres on sand, at double energy cost, plus two failed samples at 3 each, used most of the spare energy. Once d2 appeared, I had to choose between it and t2 plus a safe return. Running the battery to zero would have scored 0, so I chose t2 and base.\n\n**What worked:**\n- **Delay and noise:** position fixes averaged over several stationary ticks, with a heading-bias estimate, were accurate enough for the t2 sample and for parking at base.\n- **Battery accounting:** I tracked energy tick by tick, so the rover never got close to running out.","time":{"start":1794628684935,"end":1794628684943}}}
